change.title: pr-107534-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Template variables and ad hoc filters now get applied 2–3 times per query
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` and puts the result in the sub-requests. It keeps `scopedVars` and `filters` on those sub-requests, because it builds them with `{ ...request, targets }` (lines 315, 337, 344, 174). Each sub-request then goes through `datasource.runQuery` → `super.query`, and `DataSourceWithBackend` calls `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target again (packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185).

The shard path makes it worse. `runShardSplitQuery` applies it once (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52), then hands each shard sub-request (`{ ...request, ... }`, line 154) to `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which applies it a second time, and `super.query` applies it a third time. The test at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 expects 5 calls (1 + 4 sub-requests) even with `runQuery` mocked, which confirms the repeat.

What this does:
- Ad hoc filters on a parsed label (a query with a parser where every selector already has a matcher) go through `addFilterAsLabelFilter` (modifyQuery.ts:511-541). That function has no duplicate check, unlike `addFilterToStreamSelector` (modifyQuery.ts:494). So the query sent to Loki ends up as `{a="b"} | logfmt | level=`error` | level=`error` | level=`error``. The rows returned are the same, but the query text users see in the inspector grows, and Loki runs extra pipeline stages for every shard and chunk.
- `templateSrv.replace` now runs again on an expression whose values were already filled in. If a variable value itself contains a `$name`, `${name}` or `[[name]]` token, it gets expanded a second time. The query then changes with no error shown to the user.

Before this change, `runSplitQuery` did not interpolate anything. The shard path called `interpolateVariablesInQueries` without filters (datasource.ts:429-447), so ad hoc filters were added only once, in `super.query`.

Suggested fix: use the interpolated copy only for the decisions that need resolved values (`querySupportsSplitting`, `isLogsQuery`, the `calculateStep` grouping, `getSelectorForShardValues`). The second option is to drop `filters` from the sub-requests once they have been applied. Either way, ad hoc filters and interpolation run once per query.

findings.title: Interpolation tests rely on a `replace` mock that fills in `$__auto`, which the real code leaves alone
findings.body:
The new tests (here and in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:85-100) mock `templateSrv.replace` so it swaps `$__auto` for `5m` whatever scopedVars it gets. The real `applyTemplateVariables` deliberately removes `__auto` from the scopedVars and leaves it for the backend to interpolate (datasource.ts:1111-1113). So the assertion `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])` describes behaviour production never has. The test still passes if `applyTemplateVariables` is called with the wrong scopedVars.

The value of this change is that `step: '$step'` gets resolved before `calculateStep` groups the queries (querySplitting.ts:327-329). A test that uses a real dashboard variable (for example `$step` resolved through scopedVars) and checks the step-based grouping or partition would cover that. Also, neither test checks that ad hoc filters (`request.filters`) are passed through or applied only once.

contracts.action: runSplitQuery interpolates targets via datasource.applyTemplateVariables before partitioning and executing
contracts.equivalent_path: Non-split path: LokiDatasource.query → runQuery → DataSourceWithBackend.query, which applies applyTemplateVariables once per target (DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185).
contracts.before_after: The non-split path interpolates exactly once, inside super.query. The new path interpolates in runSplitQuery, keeps scopedVars/filters on the sub-requests ({...request, targets}), and runQuery → super.query interpolates again. So ad hoc filters and templateSrv.replace run twice.
contracts.visible_effect: Sub-requests carry the interpolated expr/step. Step grouping now sees resolved step values, and the query sent to Loki may contain duplicated ad hoc label-filter stages (addFilterAsLabelFilter has no duplicate check). Users see this in the query inspector.
contracts.failure_mode: Synchronous; if applyTemplateVariables throws (e.g. addLabelToQuery with an empty key), the error comes from runSplitQuery before the Observable exists, the same as it would from super.query.

contracts.action: runShardSplitQuery replaces interpolateVariablesInQueries (no filters) with applyTemplateVariables (with request.filters)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous implementation: interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets, scopedVars). This used the full scopedVars, added no ad hoc filters, set datasource to getRef(), and left step/legendFormat alone (datasource.ts:429-447).
contracts.before_after: Before: interpolated once without ad hoc filters, then once more in super.query. After: applyTemplateVariables with filters here, again in runSplitQuery (line 163 passes {...request} with filters), and again in super.query, so three passes. $__auto/$__interval/$__range are no longer interpolated in the frontend. The selector used for fetchLabelValues now includes ad hoc stream filters. query.datasource is no longer overwritten with getRef(); DataSourceWithBackend falls back to this datasource when it is unset.
contracts.visible_effect: Shard values are fetched for the selector including ad hoc filters. Queries may carry duplicated parsed-label filter stages. Step is now resolved.
contracts.failure_mode: fetchLabelValues failures are already caught and fall back to an unsharded group (shardQuerySplitting.ts:270-275); not changed here.

summary: The change interpolates Loki queries before time and shard splitting, so resolved `step` and expression values reach the step grouping and the shard-selector logic. It does not stop the existing interpolation in `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, and the shard path hands sub-requests to `runSplitQuery`, which interpolates again. As a result, template variables and ad hoc filters are applied twice on the split path and three times on the shard path. Ad hoc filters on parsed labels have no duplicate check, so they show up repeated in the query sent to Loki. A variable value that contains a variable token gets expanded more than once. The new tests depend on a `replace` mock that fills in `$__auto`, which the real code deliberately leaves for the backend. The PR body ("Advanced Query Processing Architecture") says nothing specific about the change.
